oracle.rationale: Approved ANC-083 v3 pass fixture: one phase validation method that visits every bead under the phase epic is the directive itself.
oracle.text: The phase validation method visits every bead under the phase epic.

oracle.text: The phase validation method skips a bead under the phase epic.

oracle.rationale: Compliant paraphrase of the quote 'One validation method that covers all beads in the phase': one command, all beads of the phase.
oracle.text: Provide one command, `atm-bd validate-phase <epic>`, that checks all beads belonging to the phase in a single pass.

oracle.rationale: Boundary: per-kind models dispatched from one method are still a single validation method; INTENT phase-bj v1 states 'a pydantic model per bead kind validates the whole phase'. Per-kind models are not multiple validation methods.
oracle.text: Add `validate_phase()`, which walks every bead under the phase epic and checks each one against the pydantic model for its bead kind (sprint, dev, fix, sanity, qa, stack).

oracle.rationale: Exception/boundary: the statement scopes coverage to beads 'in the phase'; leaving other phases' beads out is not a conflict.
oracle.text: `validate_phase()` validates every bead under the phase epic and ignores beads that belong to other phases.

oracle.rationale: Silence: the item changes bead schema validation (in scope) but says nothing about a single method or coverage of every bead; silence is not conflict.
oracle.text: Add a pydantic model for the qa bead kind that requires the branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty fields.

oracle.rationale: Topical-only: mentions bead validation but states neither one method nor coverage of every bead in the phase, and rules out neither.
oracle.text: Add bead schema validation to atm-bd-orchestration so malformed beads are caught early.

oracle.rationale: Direct conflict: several separate methods and explicitly no method that validates the whole phase, contrary to 'a single validation method must validate every bead in the phase'.
oracle.text: Give each bead kind its own validation command (validate-sprint, validate-dev, validate-qa); the lead runs whichever applies, and there is no phase-wide validation.

oracle.text: Sprint-family beads are validated by `validate_family()` and the stack bead by a separate `validate_stack()` check, with no single entry point that covers both.

oracle.rationale: Boundary on 'every': a single method exists but leaves beads of the phase unvalidated, which cannot be reconciled with 'validate every bead in the phase'.
oracle.text: One `validate_phase()` method checks the sprint and dev beads under the phase epic; sanity, qa and stack beads are not validated.

data.explanation: Oracle of 11 authority-derived cases (approved pass/fail fixtures plus paraphrase, per-kind-dispatch and out-of-phase boundary, silent, topical-only, two conflict, partial-coverage boundary and irrelevant probes) was frozen and hashed before the first Jev call and never changed. The default planning set failed the topical-only probe (addressed unclear at 0.27 on r1, verdict underspecified, repeat unstable). Three anchor-specific role-complete candidates were each run twice on every case; all three were semantically exact and stable with zero regressions, and single_method_every_bead ranked first on confidence diagnostics (66/66 cells at or above 0.8).
data.planner_action: Review the frozen oracle and acceptance table, then write the sealed question set verbatim to the ANC-083 plan-questions record with the tuning-history JSON; production review keeps the 0.6 threshold.

criteria.no: The item does not describe one method covering every bead in the phase: it is silent about validation coverage, mentions validation only in general, uses several separate methods, or says some beads of the phase are skipped or not validated.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions a phase validation method but it is not possible to tell whether that one method covers every bead of the phase.
criteria.yes: The item names one validation method, function, command or entry point and says it checks every bead, all beads, or the whole phase.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires one validation method that validates every bead in the phase. Does `item.text` state such a method: a single method, function, command or entry point that checks all beads of the phase (for example every bead under the phase epic)? One method that checks each bead against a model or schema for its kind still counts as one method. Leaving out beads of other phases does not matter. Judge presence of this directive only, not whether the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item conflicts with one method validating every bead in the phase, including when the item is silent about it.
criteria.unclear: The item is ambiguous enough that it might describe split validation or skipped beads, but it cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item splits validation across separate methods with no single one covering every bead of the phase, or says a bead or bead kind of the phase is skipped or not validated.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan bead validation in a way that `anchor.statement` rules out? The anchor rules out two things: (1) splitting validation across several separate methods or commands with no single method that validates every bead in the phase; (2) a phase validation method that skips some beads of the phase or some bead kinds. These are not a conflict: silence about validation coverage; a general mention of validation; one method that uses a different model per bead kind; leaving out beads that belong to other phases. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system, such as console display, messaging or release work, and does not touch bead validation or bead schemas.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether it touches bead validation.
criteria.yes: The item plans or changes bead validation, a bead schema or model, a validation command or method, or which beads are validated.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor about validating the beads of an atm-bd-orchestration phase (`anchor.statement`, `anchor.scope`). Does the work described in `item.text` plan, change, or depend on how beads are validated: bead schemas or models, a validator, validation commands, or which beads of a phase get checked? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.
